written_from: IBM z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385) and z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets, read by section, not page (page numbers are not cited): the DD statement DSNAME parameter (generation data group relative numbers), the DISP parameter (normal / abnormal-termination dispositions, PASS), the EXEC COND parameter, and DFSMS 'Generation data groups' (relative generation resolution at job start, roll-in at job end, LIMIT). The expected answers were written before any evaluator ran on them. Read again 2026-11-19 from the local JCL User's Guide (ieab500_v3r1.txt, Appendix A, 'DSNAME Parameter - GDGBIAS=JOB', p. 236) and the JCL Reference (GDGBIAS parameter, p. 403: GDGBIAS=JOB is the default): the relationship between a relative and an absolute generation is fixed at the first reference in the job, a generation created by (+1) is read in a later step by the same (+1), cannot be read in its own step, and 'at the end of the job' the relative numbers of the group are updated. That answers the old assumption A1 (roll-in at the end of the job); A2 is still assumed. Read again 2026-11-20 for GDGBIAS=STEP (User's Guide Appendix A, 'Relative generation numbers' p. 235, 'DSNAME Parameter - GDGBIAS=STEP' pp. 236-237 and 238-239, Example 7 p. 246; JCL Reference JOB: GDGBIAS pp. 403-404): the relationship is established at the first reference in each job step and the catalog is updated at the end of the job step. Restarted jobs (User's Guide 'Restarting a job with generation data sets' p. 243; JCL Reference JOB: RESTART, 'Generation data sets in restarted jobs' pp. 431-432) are a later slice.
scenario_input: catalog (or catalog_from: another scenario's catalog_after): per GDG base, limit and the cataloged absolute generations, oldest first. given: per step that starts, {rc: n} or {abend: code}.
scenario_answer: expect: per STEP.DDNAME of each step that runs, the absolute generation number the DD names. catalog_after: per base the cataloged generations, oldest first, after the job ends.
flow_jcl: //* #8413 slice 3: GDG relative generations. Which absolute generation
//* each DD names, and the catalog after the job. The answers are in
//* scenarios.json, written from IBM's z/OS MVS JCL Reference
//* (SA23-1385) and z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets before any
//* #8413 slice 5: GDGBIAS=STEP, and GDG DDs inside procedure steps.

scenarios.basis: DSNAME, generation data group: (0) is the most recent generation cataloged, (-1) the one before it, (-2) the one before that. With generations 5, 6, 7 cataloged, (0) = 7, (-1) = 6, (-2) = 5. Reading creates nothing, so the catalog is unchanged.

DSNAME: (+1) names the next generation, 8. Every relative number in a job is resolved against the catalog as it stood when the job started, so (+1) in the later step C2 is the same generation C1 created, while (0) is still 7 and (-1) is still 6 (the new generation is not rolled into the catalog until the job ends). At job end 8 is cataloged as the most recent.
A later job sees the catalog the earlier job left: 8 is now (0), 7 is (-1), 6 is (-2).

DSNAME: (+1) is the next generation after the one current at job start (2), so 3; (+2) is the one after that, 4. A later step naming (+1) or (+2) names those same generations; (0) is still 2. Both are cataloged at job end, oldest first.

DISP, abnormal-termination disposition: EOUT is DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE) and E1 abends, so generation 8 is deleted and never cataloged; the PAY.GDG catalog is unchanged. E2 (COND=EVEN) runs after the abend and ends normally, so its (+1) of AUD.GDG, 3, is cataloged.

DISP: when the abnormal-termination disposition is omitted the system applies the normal-termination one. FOUT is DISP=(NEW,CATLG) and E2 abends, so generation 3 is cataloged anyway. E1 ends normally, 8 is cataloged.
EXEC COND: B1 ends RC 8, so (4,LT,B1) is true and B2 is bypassed; a bypassed step allocates none of its DDs, so BOUT creates nothing. B3's (+1) is 8 and is cataloged at job end.
DISP PASS: the generation created by P1 is passed to P2 under the same (+1) name; P2's DISP=(OLD,CATLG) catalogs it, so 8 is cataloged.

Generation data group LIMIT: the group holds at most LIMIT generations (3). Rolling 8 in makes the oldest, 5, drop out of the catalog; whether 5 is also scratched (deleted) depends on the group's SCRATCH / NOSCRATCH attribute and is not answered here. Relative numbers in the job are unchanged by the limit.

DISP, generation data sets (User's Guide, Appendix A, 'DISP parameter'): if you code MOD for a generation data set and the specified relative generation does not exist in the catalog, the system changes the status to NEW. (+1) is not cataloged, so M1's MOUT is a NEW generation, 8, cataloged at job end. M2's MADD names (0), which exists (7), so it stays MOD: it names 7 and creates nothing, and the group's relative numbers are unchanged until job end.
DISP MOD on the absent (+1) is changed to NEW (see mod-plus-one-creates-a-generation), so the DD names generation 8; N1 abends and the abnormal disposition DELETE applies, so 8 is not cataloged.

z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets, chapter 29 'Processing generation data groups', 'Relative generation number': the absolute number assigned depends on the number last assigned (7) and the relative number (+2), and 'if you have a single step job, and the generation being cataloged is a +2, one generation number is skipped' (8). So S1.SOUT names 9 and 9 is cataloged at job end; 8 is never cataloged.

z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets, chapter 29 'Processing generation data groups', 'Relative generation number': a relative number 'tells the system the location of an entry representing a previously cataloged generation'. The catalog holds 5, 6, 7, 9, so (0) = 9 and (-1) is the entry before it, 7, not the missing 8; (-2) = 6. ASSUMED (A4): the manual says 'location of an entry' but never works an example across a skipped number.

z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets, chapter 29 'Processing generation data groups', 'Rolling In a Generation Data Set': 'If a GDG is defined using DEFINE GENERATIONDATAGROUP EMPTY, and is at its limit, then, when a new generation data set is rolled in, all the currently active generation data sets are rolled off.' The group holds 3 of its limit 3, so the roll-in at the end-of-job step leaves only 8. The names in the job are resolved at job start, as in create-then-read-same-job.

z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets, chapter 29 'Processing generation data groups', 'Rolling In a Generation Data Set': EMPTY empties the group only when it 'is at its limit'. It holds 2 of 3, so 8 is rolled in and nothing rolls off.

z/OS DFSMS Using Data Sets, chapter 29 'Processing generation data groups', 'Rolling In a Generation Data Set': 'Generation data sets can be in a deferred roll-in state if ... they are allocated with a DISP=(NEW,KEEP)', and 'Refer to generation data sets that are in a deferred roll-in state by their relative number, such as (+1), within the job that allocates it.' So K2 reads (+1) = 8, the generation K1 kept; 8 is not rolled into the active group at job end (the active generations stay 5, 6, 7) and waits, to be named by its absolute number in a later job. ASSUMED (A5): the group is system-managed, which is the case the manual's deferred roll-in text describes.

z/OS MVS JCL User's Guide, Appendix A 'Generation data sets', 'Deleting and uncataloging generation data sets' (the manual's first worked example, GDGBIAS=JOB, generations G0006, G0007, G0008 exist): 'the absolute generation number that is referenced by relative generation number in STEP1 (DD1) is G0007V00. The system establishes the relative/absolute relationship that it maintains throughout the job. In STEP2, all generation data sets are to be deleted, which occurs at STEP2 termination. In STEP3, the system assigns the absolute generation number G0009V00 to the new generation data set'. So Q1IN names 7, Q2DEL (a DD of the base name) deletes 6, 7 and 8 at step end, Q3OUT names 9, and 9 is the only cataloged generation after the job.

z/OS MVS JCL User's Guide, Appendix A 'Generation data sets', 'Deleting and uncataloging generation data sets' (the manual's second worked example: 'the JCL is set up to delete all generation data sets at the beginning of the job'): 'the system establishes the relative/absolute relationship in STEP2, the first time that a relative generation number is used in the job. The system then assigns absolute generation number G0001V00 to the data set referenced in DD2 and absolute generation number G0002V00 to the data set referenced in DD3.' So R2OUT names 1, R3OUT names 2, and both are rolled in at job end.

z/OS MVS JCL User's Guide, Appendix A 'Generation data sets', 'Deleting and uncataloging generation data sets': 'If a DD statement in a multiple-step job tries to delete or uncatalog any generation data set except the oldest in a GDG, catalog management can lose orientation within the data group', so deleting the oldest is the form the manual leaves safe. O1 names (-2) = 6 (the oldest of 6, 7, 8) and establishes the relationship, which 'the system maintains throughout the job' (the same text as the first worked example): O2 still reads (0) = 8 and (-1) = 7, and 6 is gone from the catalog at O1 termination. ASSUMED (A6): the manual works no example that deletes a single generation, so that the entry is removed and nothing else changes is read from the DISP text, not from an example.

z/OS MVS JCL User's Guide (SA23-0393 / ieab500), Appendix A, 'Relative generation numbers' p. 235: 'When you are using GDGBIAS=STEP, relative references to a generation data set are resolved on a job step basis. The system establishes the relationship between the relative generation number and the absolute generation number when the generation data set is first referenced in each job step. Each job step that references the generation data set establishes a new relationship.' (the same text: z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385 / ieab600), JOB, GDGBIAS, p. 404). 'DSNAME Parameter - GDGBIAS=STEP' pp. 236-237: 'At the end of the job step, the system updates the catalog with the relative generation numbers of all generations in the group to reflect the additions.' Example 7 p. 246 (GDGBIAS=STEP, STEP1 DD A DSNAME=GDG01(+1),DISP=(NEW,CATLG); STEP2 DD B DSNAME=GDG01(0)): 'DD statement A - create 1st generation (and catalog at end of step). DD statement B - reference 1st generation.' With 5, 6, 7 cataloged, A creates 8, rolled in at the end of S1; S2 first references the group, so its (0) is the newest generation then cataloged, 8 (under the job basis the same (0) is 7: see job-bias-named-is-the-default).

z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385 / ieab600), JOB, GDGBIAS, pp. 403-404: JOB 'establishes the relationship between the relative generation number and the absolute generation number when the generation data set is first referenced in the job. This relationship is consistent throughout the job.' 'If no GDGBIAS parameter is specified ... GDGBIAS=JOB is used' (when the job class names no default). The same JCL as step-bias-create-then-read-zero with GDGBIAS=JOB: A first references the group (0 = 7), so B's (0) is still 7, and 8 is added at the end of the job (UG p. 236). Naming JOB is the same as naming nothing.

z/OS MVS JCL User's Guide (SA23-0393 / ieab500), Appendix A, 'Relative generation numbers' p. 235: 'When you are using GDGBIAS=STEP, relative references to a generation data set are resolved on a job step basis. The system establishes the relationship between the relative generation number and the absolute generation number when the generation data set is first referenced in each job step. Each job step that references the generation data set establishes a new relationship.' (the same text: z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385 / ieab600), JOB, GDGBIAS, p. 404). 'DSNAME Parameter - GDGBIAS=STEP' pp. 236-237: 'At the end of the job step, the system updates the catalog with the relative generation numbers of all generations in the group to reflect the additions.' 'Each job step that references the generation data set establishes a new relationship': T1's (+1) is 8 and 8 is rolled into the group at the end of T1; T2 establishes a new relationship against the catalog that now ends at 8, so its (+1) is 9 (under GDGBIAS=JOB the second (+1) would be the same generation as the first, UG p. 235, so the JOB basis must write (+2): the refused list names the job-basis twin). T3 sees 5, 6, 7, 8, 9: (0) = 9, (-1) = 8.

z/OS MVS JCL User's Guide (SA23-0393 / ieab500), Appendix A, 'Relative generation numbers' p. 235: 'When you are using GDGBIAS=STEP, relative references to a generation data set are resolved on a job step basis. The system establishes the relationship between the relative generation number and the absolute generation number when the generation data set is first referenced in each job step. Each job step that references the generation data set establishes a new relationship.' (the same text: z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385 / ieab600), JOB, GDGBIAS, p. 404). 'DSNAME Parameter - GDGBIAS=STEP' pp. 236-237: 'At the end of the job step, the system updates the catalog with the relative generation numbers of all generations in the group to reflect the additions.' The roll-in happens at step termination (UG 'Disposition of SMS-managed generation data sets' p. 237: 'At step termination, the deferred generation data set is rolled into the GDG base'), so with LIMIT 3 generation 5 is rolled off before L2 starts (the roll-off of the oldest at the limit is as in limit-rolls-off-oldest). L2's group is 6, 7, 8: (0) = 8 and (-2) = 6; under the job basis (-2) would still be 5.

z/OS MVS JCL User's Guide (SA23-0393 / ieab500), Appendix A, 'Relative generation numbers' p. 235: 'When you are using GDGBIAS=STEP, relative references to a generation data set are resolved on a job step basis. The system establishes the relationship between the relative generation number and the absolute generation number when the generation data set is first referenced in each job step. Each job step that references the generation data set establishes a new relationship.' (the same text: z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385 / ieab600), JOB, GDGBIAS, p. 404). 'DSNAME Parameter - GDGBIAS=STEP' pp. 236-237: 'At the end of the job step, the system updates the catalog with the relative generation numbers of all generations in the group to reflect the additions.' B1's 8 is rolled in when B1 ends, before B2 starts; B2's (+1) is a new relationship, 9. B2 abends under DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE): the abnormal disposition applies (DISP, abnormal termination) so 9 is deleted, not cataloged. The job ends with 5, 6, 7, 8: under the job basis the roll-in waits for the job end and the same JCL is not asked.

z/OS MVS JCL User's Guide (SA23-0393 / ieab500), Appendix A, p. 235 (GDGBIAS=JOB, the default, REF p. 404): the relationship is fixed at the first reference in the job and 'any subsequent reference to (+1) throughout the job' is the same absolute generation. The first reference is the DD OUT of procedure step M1 (called as C1): (+1) = 8; R1's (+1) names the same generation; the job's later step C2 still reads (0) as 7 and 8 is added at the end of the job. ASSUMED (A7): the manual states GDGBIAS for 'a job step' and is silent on a procedure's steps; they are executed as steps of the job (JCL Reference, DD: 'a job step, in a cataloged procedure step, or in an in-stream procedure step').

z/OS MVS JCL User's Guide (SA23-0393 / ieab500), Appendix A, 'Relative generation numbers' p. 235: 'When you are using GDGBIAS=STEP, relative references to a generation data set are resolved on a job step basis. The system establishes the relationship between the relative generation number and the absolute generation number when the generation data set is first referenced in each job step. Each job step that references the generation data set establishes a new relationship.' (the same text: z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385 / ieab600), JOB, GDGBIAS, p. 404). 'DSNAME Parameter - GDGBIAS=STEP' pp. 236-237: 'At the end of the job step, the system updates the catalog with the relative generation numbers of all generations in the group to reflect the additions.' Each procedure step is a job step for the new relationship (ASSUMED A7, as in proc-step-gdg-dds-are-job-steps): C1.M1 creates (+1) = 8 and 8 is rolled in at its end; C1.R1 first references the group and reads (0) = 8; the second call C2 runs the same procedure text: C2.M1's (+1) is 9 and C2.R1's (0) is 9. The procedure's JCL is the same for both calls; the answers differ because the catalog at each step differs.

z/OS MVS JCL User's Guide (SA23-0393 / ieab500), Appendix A, 'Restarting a job with generation data sets' p. 243 'For step restart', and z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385 / ieab600), JOB: RESTART, 'Generation data sets in restarted jobs' p. 431 (JCL Reference p. 431): 'if the last generation data set created and cataloged was assigned a generation number of +2, it would be referred to as 0 in the restart step and in steps following the restart step. ... the generation data set assigned number of +1 when created would be referred to as -1.' The first run (catalog 6, 7) created and cataloged 8 (+1) and 9 (+2) in STEP1 and STEP2, so the restart, which begins at STEP3, finds 6, 7, 8, 9 cataloged: its (0) is 9 and its (-1) is 8. STEP1 and STEP2 do not run again.

z/OS MVS JCL User's Guide (SA23-0393 / ieab500), Appendix A, 'Restarting a job with generation data sets' p. 243: after a step restart the generations cataloged before the restart step are named by their present numbers. The restart finds 6, 7, 8, 9 cataloged, so a (+1) created in the restart step STEP3 is 10 (DSNAME: (+1) is the next generation after the most recent); STEP4's (+1) is the same generation (the relationship is fixed at the first reference in the job, GDGBIAS=JOB default, User's Guide p. 236), and its (0) is still 9 until the job ends, when 10 is rolled in.

z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385 / ieab600), JOB: RESTART, 'Generation data sets in restarted jobs' p. 431: RESTART=* restarts at the first step, so no step runs before the restart step and nothing was created and cataloged for the restart to renumber; the job resolves its generations against the catalog as it stands, 6, 7: (+1) is 8 and (0) is 7 until the job ends (User's Guide p. 236, GDGBIAS=JOB), as in an ordinary run.

z/OS MVS JCL User's Guide (SA23-0393 / ieab500), Appendix A, 'Restarting a job with generation data sets' p. 243 'For checkpoint restart': 'you can, during checkpoint restart, refer to these data sets and generation data sets created and cataloged in steps before the restart step by the same relative generation numbers that were used to create them.' RESTART=(STEP3,CHK1) with a SYSCHK DD is a deferred checkpoint restart (JCL Reference, JOB: RESTART examples 2-4); the manual states the same-numbers rule under 'checkpoint restart' and gives deferred restart only a volume-serial note, so applying it to the deferred form is ASSUMED A9. The original run began with 6, 7 cataloged: STEP1's (+1) is 8 and STEP2's (+2) is 9, both cataloged before the restart step, and the restart step names them by (+1) and (+2) again: 8 and 9. STEP3 creates (+3) = 10 and STEP4 reads it as (+3).

z/OS MVS JCL User's Guide (SA23-0393 / ieab500), Appendix A, 'Restarting a job with generation data sets' p. 243 'For checkpoint restart' and z/OS MVS JCL Reference (SA23-1385 / ieab600), JOB: RESTART, 'Generation data sets in restarted jobs' p. 431 (p. 432): 'If generation data sets created in the restart step were kept instead of cataloged, that is, DISP=(NEW,CATLG,KEEP) was coded, then refer to them by the same relative generation numbers used to create them.' STEP3 abends, so its abnormal disposition KEEP applies (DISP) and generation 10 is kept, not cataloged (it stays in deferred roll-in, DFSMS Using Data Sets); STEP4 (COND=EVEN runs after the abend) names it by the number that created it, (+3) = 10. Generations 8 and 9 were cataloged by the steps before the restart step. ASSUMED A9 as for the previous scenario.

assumed.text: A generation whose creating step abends under (NEW,CATLG,DELETE) is not cataloged, and under (NEW,CATLG) is, per the DISP text; the absolute number is still consumed by that job only (the next job reuses it).

After the system changes MOD to NEW on a (+n) generation, the step-end disposition is read from the coded DISP as it is for a DISP=NEW dataset; the manual states the status change but not that the abnormal-termination subparameter then applies as for NEW.
A negative relative number counts entries of the generation index, so a number skipped by a (+2) is not counted: with 5, 6, 7, 9 cataloged, (-1) is 7.
The GDG is system-managed; the manual states the deferred roll-in of NEW,KEEP only for that case.

Deleting the oldest generation by relative number (DISP=(OLD,DELETE) of (-n) where it is the oldest) removes that one catalog entry at step end and leaves the other generations' absolute numbers unchanged; the manual states only the warning for any other generation.

A procedure's step counts as a job step for GDGBIAS: the relationship is established (STEP) at its first reference of a group, and the catalog is updated at its end. The manual states GDGBIAS for 'a job step' and is silent on a procedure step; the system executes a procedure's steps as steps of the job.

A JOB statement with no GDGBIAS= resolves on a job basis. The manual (JCL Reference p. 404) makes JOB the default only for a job class that names no default; the class default is installation-defined and is not in the repository.

The same-relative-numbers rule the manuals state for checkpoint restart is applied to a deferred checkpoint restart, RESTART=(stepname,checkid) with a SYSCHK DD: the manuals give the deferred form only a volume-serial note under this heading. The catalog given for such a scenario is the catalog as the original run began, so the original relative numbers name the same generations; the steps before the restart step are taken as run to normal end.

refused.construct: two steps of one job creating the same (+n) with DISP=NEW
refused.why: the second allocation names a dataset that already exists; IBM's text for the failure is not answered here

refused.construct: a (+n) read before any step creates it, or (0) / (-n) with no such cataloged generation
refused.why: a JCL or catalog error, not a step-flow answer

refused.construct: a PASSed generation never received by a later step
refused.why: the manual's disposition of an unreceived passed dataset is not answered here

refused.construct: UNCATLG generations, absolute names (G0007V00), the SCRATCH / NOSCRATCH fate of a rolled-off generation
DISP=MOD of (0) / (-n) with that generation not cataloged, or MOD (+n) after the same (+n) was passed
refused.why: the manual says the status becomes NEW but gives no absolute number for (0) / (-n), and a MOD of a generation created earlier in the job is not stated

refused.construct: the (+1) number of a job that follows one that left a generation in deferred roll-in (NEW,KEEP)
refused.why: the manual says the number depends on 'the number last assigned' but not whether a deferred generation counts

refused.construct: a job that never reaches the end-of-job step (a CATLG generation left in deferred roll-in)
refused.why: the manual lists it as a deferred-roll-in cause; the step-flow model only ends jobs normally

refused.construct: DISP=(OLD,DELETE) of a generation other than the oldest
refused.why: the manual says catalog management can lose orientation within the data group: the outcome is not stated

refused.construct: a (0) / (-n) read of a generation deleted earlier in the job
refused.why: the generation is gone from the catalog; the manual warns not to refer to older generations after a delete and states no outcome

refused.construct: a DISP=(OLD,DELETE) of the whole group in a job that also created a generation earlier
refused.why: the manual does not say whether a generation created earlier in the job (rolled in only at job end) is part of the group deleted

refused.construct: two calls of a procedure whose step creates (+1), under GDGBIAS=JOB (or no GDGBIAS)
refused.why: UG p. 235 says each addition in the job takes the next number (+1, +2, ...): the second call's (+1) names the same generation; refused as two steps creating the same (+n)

refused.construct: GDGBIAS=STEP with a PASSed or KEEP-deferred generation of a group that a later step references
refused.why: the manual states the step-end catalog update for a cataloged generation only; a generation still passed or deferred is not part of the catalog the later step's relationship is built from

refused.construct: a GDGBIAS value other than JOB or STEP
refused.why: invalid; the JCL Reference lists only {JOB|STEP}

refused.construct: a GDG DD of a procedure step that the call overrides (stepname.ddname), a symbolic DSN, a procedure that is not in-stream, or a nested call
refused.why: this slice reads the in-stream procedure's own DD rows; the overridden or substituted DSN is not answered here

refused.construct: a step restart whose restart step or a later step reads a generation by the number that created it in a step before the restart step, for example (+1)
refused.why: JCL Reference p. 431: 'do not use the original relative generation numbers' there; the manual states no outcome, so the (+1) is refused as read before any step creates it

refused.construct: a checkpoint restart (RESTART=(step,checkid)) of a job with GDGBIAS=STEP, or whose steps before the restart step do not create their (+n) with NEW / MOD
refused.why: the manuals state the checkpoint rule by the numbers that created the generations, not how a per-step relationship is rebuilt; refused by name
